Orchard Growers Join Forces to Reach City Shoppers

DELMONT (August 28)—Apple growers in the Delmont Valley have found a new way to sell
their fruit. Last spring, eleven family-owned orchards formed the Delmont Valley Growers
Cooperative, which now delivers fresh produce directly to grocery stores in Carlisle, a city
about 90 kilometers to the east. — [1] —.

Before the cooperative was formed, most of the farms sold their harvest to large
distributors at low prices. "On our own, none of us could afford refrigerated trucks," said
Martin Ellery, who runs a 40-acre orchard and serves as the cooperative's president. "By
sharing the cost, we can now transport our apples ourselves." — [2] —.

The arrangement appears to be working. Ellery said the members' earnings rose by an
average of 20 percent in the first season. Three Carlisle supermarkets currently carry the
cooperative's products, and a fourth chain has expressed interest. — [3] —.

The cooperative plans to begin selling pears and cider next year. — [4] —. Growers outside
the valley who wish to join may contact the cooperative through its Web site.
